questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: opioids brainstem respiratory depression slows heart
questions.text: AHA Part 9 explains how an opioid overdose progresses to cardiac arrest. Which mechanism does the manual describe?

answers.text: Opioids affect the brainstem, suppress the drive to breathe, and can slow the heart rate leading to arrest
Opioids directly damage kidney tissue causing cardiac arrest
Opioids stimulate the heart to beat too fast
Opioids block oxygen absorption directly in the lungs

explanations.a: AHA Part 9 says opioids affect the brainstem which controls breathing; high doses suppress the natural drive to breathe, slow the heart rate, and can lead to cardiac arrest.
explanations.b: Kidney damage is not the AHA-described mechanism for opioid cardiac arrest.
explanations.c: Opioids slow rather than stimulate the heart, primarily through respiratory depression.
explanations.d: Opioids do not block oxygen absorption in the lungs; the failure is in the central drive to breathe.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: naloxone safe even if not sure drug taken
questions.text: An adult is unresponsive with slow shallow breathing after a suspected drug exposure, and naloxone is available. AHA Part 9 makes a key safety point. Which statement matches?

answers.text: Naloxone should be withheld unless the rescuer is sure of the drug taken
Naloxone is safe to administer even if you're not sure what drug the person took
Naloxone reverses all known overdoses regardless of the substance
Naloxone is reserved for ALS-only administration

explanations.a: Withholding naloxone while diagnostic certainty is sought delays reversal.
explanations.b: AHA Part 9 explicitly says naloxone is safe to administer even if you are not sure what drug the person took.
explanations.c: Naloxone specifically reverses opioid effects; it does not reverse all overdoses.
explanations.d: Naloxone is available without a prescription in many jurisdictions and can be administered by lay rescuers.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: second dose 2 to 3 minutes no response
questions.text: After giving an initial dose of naloxone, the person does not respond. According to AHA Part 9, what is the interval before a second dose may be given?

answers.text: Give a second dose if the person does not respond within 2 to 3 minutes
Never give a second dose
Give a second dose after 30 minutes
Give 5 doses immediately in succession

explanations.a: AHA Part 9 says given the potency of opiates, you may need to give a second dose if the person does not respond within 2 to 3 minutes after the first dose.
explanations.b: A second dose is sometimes necessary; never giving one is not the AHA position.
explanations.c: Thirty minutes is too long given the potency of opioids.
explanations.d: Stacking 5 immediate doses is not the AHA recommendation.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: routes IV IM intranasal
questions.text: Per AHA Part 9, naloxone may be administered by which routes during an opioid emergency?

answers.text: Intravenously, intramuscularly, and intranasally
Only by mouth
Only as a continuous IV infusion
Only via subcutaneous injection in the abdomen

explanations.a: AHA Part 9 lists intravenous, intramuscular, and intranasal as common routes for naloxone administration.
explanations.b: Oral naloxone is destroyed by first-pass metabolism and is not used for opioid reversal.
explanations.c: BLS naloxone is given as a single dose via standard routes, not as a continuous infusion.
explanations.d: Subcutaneous abdominal injection is not the AHA-recommended route.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: autoinjector single dose intramuscular IM
questions.text: AHA Part 9 describes naloxone handheld autoinjectors. How does the manual characterize their action?

answers.text: Naloxone autoinjectors deliver a single dose via an intramuscular injection
Autoinjectors deliver a continuous IV infusion
Autoinjectors deliver naloxone via the eye
Autoinjectors deliver oral tablets through a spring mechanism

explanations.a: AHA Part 9 says naloxone handheld autoinjectors deliver a single dose via an intramuscular injection.
explanations.b: Autoinjectors are not infusion devices; they deliver a single fixed dose.
explanations.c: Eye administration is not used for naloxone delivery.
explanations.d: Naloxone autoinjectors deliver intramuscularly, not as oral tablets.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: naloxone nalmefene two antagonists robust data naloxone
questions.text: AHA Part 9 names two opioid antagonists available in the United States. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: Only naloxone is approved; nalmefene does not exist
Only nalmefene is approved for opioid reversal
Atropine and epinephrine are the standard opioid antagonists
Naloxone and nalmefene are both available; published clinical data are more robust for naloxone

explanations.a: AHA Part 9 names both naloxone and nalmefene as available antagonists.
explanations.b: Naloxone is the more widely used and studied of the two.
explanations.c: Atropine and epinephrine are not opioid antagonists; they are used for different indications.
explanations.d: AHA Part 9 names naloxone and nalmefene as the two opioid antagonists available, noting that to date the published clinical data are more robust for naloxone.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: chest discomfort squeezing pressure heaviness
questions.text: AHA Part 10 describes the typical type of chest discomfort in a heart attack. Which description matches?

answers.text: Sharp stabbing pain that lasts 2 seconds
Discomfort that may feel like squeezing, pressure, fullness, or pain in the chest
Burning pain relieved immediately by lying down
Itching over the entire chest that spreads to the legs

explanations.a: Sharp stabbing pain lasting 2 seconds is more suggestive of musculoskeletal chest pain than cardiac.
explanations.b: AHA Part 10 describes heart attack chest discomfort as possibly feeling like squeezing, pressure, fullness, or pain in the center or left side of the chest.
explanations.c: Burning relieved by lying down is more consistent with reflux.
explanations.d: Itching spreading to the legs is not the AHA description of heart attack discomfort.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: upper body discomfort left arm back neck jaw
questions.text: AHA Part 10 lists possible sites of upper-body discomfort in a heart attack. Which set matches?

answers.text: Left arm commonly, and possibly both arms, upper back, neck, jaw, or stomach
Lower back below the waist only
Right ankle only
Toes and feet only

explanations.a: AHA Part 10 describes upper-body discomfort that can include the left arm commonly, and also both arms, the upper back, neck, jaw, or stomach.
explanations.b: Isolated lower back pain below the waist is not the AHA-listed pattern.
explanations.c: Right ankle pain is not on the AHA list of heart attack symptoms.
explanations.d: Foot and toe pain are not on the AHA list of heart attack symptoms.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: aspirin 162 to 325 mg chew swallow no allergy
questions.text: An alert adult on a sidewalk is having chest pain you suspect is a heart attack. According to AHA Part 10, what aspirin dose should you encourage if there is no known allergy?

answers.text: 5 to 10 mg of aspirin
5000 mg of aspirin
1000 mg of aspirin
162 to 325 mg of aspirin

explanations.a: 5 to 10 mg is far below the AHA-specified dose.
explanations.b: 5000 mg is a toxic dose far above the AHA recommendation.
explanations.c: 1000 mg exceeds the AHA-recommended range without added benefit.
explanations.d: AHA Part 10 says encourage the alert adult to chew and swallow 162 to 325 mg of aspirin unless they have a known aspirin allergy or have been told not to take it.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: withhold aspirin known allergy or told not to take
questions.text: A person experiencing chest pain tells you they are allergic to aspirin. According to AHA Part 10, what is appropriate?

answers.text: Give aspirin anyway because the benefit outweighs the risk
Give double the normal dose to overcome any allergic reaction
Give ibuprofen as a substitute
Withhold aspirin and let advanced care decide upon arrival

explanations.a: AHA Part 10 explicitly states aspirin should not be given if the person has a known aspirin allergy.
explanations.b: Doubling the dose worsens the allergic reaction risk.
explanations.c: Ibuprofen is not a substitute for aspirin in suspected heart attack and is not part of AHA BLS guidance.
explanations.d: AHA Part 10 directs withholding aspirin for known allergy and deferring to advanced care.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: call 911 act fast minutes matter heart attack
questions.text: AHA Part 10 emphasizes that a heart attack requires immediate action. Which approach matches the manual?

answers.text: Drive the person to the hospital yourself to save time
Wait and see if the pain resolves in the next hour
Call 911 and activate EMS so the person receives care as soon as possible
Give the person water and encourage them to walk around

explanations.a: Self-transport delays care and puts the driver and patient at risk if the person's condition worsens.
explanations.b: Waiting in a suspected heart attack can allow permanent myocardial damage to extend.
explanations.c: AHA Part 10 says call 911 immediately — every minute a coronary artery is blocked, more heart muscle is at risk.
explanations.d: Walking and water do not treat a heart attack.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: FAST face arm speech time 911
questions.text: AHA Part 10 teaches F.A.S.T. to recognize stroke warning signs. What do the four letters stand for?

answers.text: Fever, Aches, Sneezing, Tiredness
Fall, Aspirin, Sit, Treatment
Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911
Fast, Active, Strong, Talking

explanations.a: These are general viral illness symptoms, not stroke warning signs.
explanations.b: These do not match the AHA F.A.S.T. acronym.
explanations.c: AHA Part 10 says F.A.S.T. stands for Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call 911.
explanations.d: These do not match the AHA F.A.S.T. acronym.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: time critical every minute more brain tissue dies
questions.text: AHA Part 10 describes stroke as a 'time-critical' emergency. Which statement best summarizes the rationale?

answers.text: Every minute counts because more brain tissue dies as treatment is delayed
Stroke patients can wait days for treatment without consequence
Stroke only matters if the person is over 80 years old
Stroke care does not depend on the time of symptom onset

explanations.a: AHA Part 10 says stroke is a time-critical emergency where every minute counts — every minute treatment is delayed, more brain tissue dies.
explanations.b: Days of delay would result in massive irreversible brain injury.
explanations.c: Stroke can occur at any adult age and treatment matters at all ages.
explanations.d: Time of symptom onset is a key factor guiding stroke treatment and triage decisions.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: triage stroke center comprehensive thrombectomy primary
questions.text: AHA Part 10 describes how stroke patients should be transported by EMS. Which triage approach matches?

answers.text: Always transport to the nearest hospital regardless of capabilities
Family should drive the patient to avoid EMS delays
Triage to the nearest appropriate facility, which may include Comprehensive, Thrombectomy-Capable, Primary, or Acute Stroke Ready Hospitals
Tell the patient to wait at home for symptoms to clear

explanations.a: Going to the nearest hospital without considering stroke capabilities can delay essential treatments like thrombectomy.
explanations.b: Family transport delays definitive care and is not part of the AHA stroke pathway.
explanations.c: AHA Part 10 says the patient should be triaged to the nearest appropriate facility for stroke care — choices may include Comprehensive Stroke Centers, Thrombectomy-Capable Stroke Centers, Primary Stroke Centers, or Acute Stroke Ready Hospitals.
explanations.d: Stroke is not a 'wait it out' condition; immediate evaluation is essential.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: TIA transient ischemic attack warning same symptoms
questions.text: AHA Part 10 mentions transient ischemic attack (TIA). Which statement matches the manual's characterization?

answers.text: A TIA is a permanent stroke with full recovery
A TIA produces symptoms similar to stroke that typically resolve within 24 hours and is a warning sign requiring immediate evaluation
A TIA only affects people over 80 and has no further risk
A TIA requires no medical follow-up if symptoms resolve

explanations.a: A TIA is transient and does not result in permanent neurologic deficit, unlike a stroke.
explanations.b: AHA Part 10 describes TIA as producing stroke-like symptoms that typically resolve within 24 hours, and notes it is an important warning sign requiring immediate medical evaluation.
explanations.c: TIA can occur at any age and carries significant risk of subsequent stroke.
explanations.d: TIA requires urgent evaluation even if symptoms resolve, because stroke risk is highest in the days following a TIA.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: everyone transported ED alert or not
questions.text: After an apparently successful rescue from near-drowning, the rescued person seems alert. According to AHA Part 10, what is the recommended action?

answers.text: Discharge the person at the scene if they appear normal
Transport only if the person needed full CPR
Provide aspirin and send the person home
Anyone who has experienced drowning should be transported to the ED for evaluation, even those who appear to have recovered

explanations.a: Apparently normal status at the scene does not rule out delayed pulmonary or neurologic complications.
explanations.b: Transport is recommended even when only breaths were needed, not just when CPR was performed.
explanations.c: Aspirin is not a treatment for drowning.
explanations.d: AHA Part 10 says anyone who has experienced drowning should be transported by EMS to the ED for evaluation and monitoring, including people who needed only breaths and those who seem to have recovered.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: no abdominal thrusts to remove water not recommended dangerous
questions.text: A bystander asks whether they should perform abdominal thrusts to expel water from the lungs of a drowning victim before starting CPR. What does AHA Part 10 say?

answers.text: Yes — abdominal thrusts effectively remove water from the lungs
Use 10 abdominal thrusts before any breaths
Do not use abdominal thrusts to try to remove water — they are not recommended and can be dangerous
Always invert the victim by the ankles to drain water

explanations.a: AHA explicitly excludes abdominal thrusts as a water-removal technique.
explanations.b: Abdominal thrusts before breaths are not part of the drowning resuscitation sequence.
explanations.c: AHA Part 10 says do not use abdominal thrusts to try to remove water from the breathing passages — these actions are not recommended and can be dangerous.
explanations.d: Inverting the victim wastes time and can cause aspiration of stomach contents.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: drowning CPR breaths critical respiratory cause
questions.text: AHA Part 10 explains why rescue breaths are especially important for drowning victims. Which reason matches?

answers.text: Drowning arrests are primarily cardiac in origin so only compressions are needed
Breaths are less important than compressions in all arrests
Drowning victims have adequate oxygen reserves for 30 minutes
Drowning arrests are primarily due to respiratory causes, so early rescue breaths are critical

explanations.a: Drowning arrests are primarily respiratory, not cardiac, so compressions alone are less effective.
explanations.b: For arrests with respiratory causes — including drowning — ventilation is critical alongside compressions.
explanations.c: Drowning victims suffer hypoxia, not oxygen reserves.
explanations.d: AHA Part 10 emphasizes that because drowning arrests are typically due to respiratory causes, early breaths are critical in addition to compressions.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: two or more body systems involved
questions.text: AHA Part 10 helps rescuers recognize anaphylaxis. Which characteristic of the presentation does the manual highlight?

answers.text: Anaphylaxis affects only the skin
Two or more body systems are involved
Anaphylaxis is limited to changes in heart rate alone
Anaphylaxis affects only the digestive system

explanations.a: Skin signs alone are common in mild allergic reactions; anaphylaxis involves multiple systems.
explanations.b: AHA Part 10 says in anaphylaxis, two or more body systems are involved.
explanations.c: Heart rate changes are part of the picture but not the sole feature.
explanations.d: Anaphylaxis is multi-system; isolated digestive involvement is not the AHA description.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: epinephrine autoinjector side of thigh halfway hip knee
questions.text: A coworker with a known allergy develops hives, wheezing, and dizziness. They have an epinephrine autoinjector. AHA Part 10 specifies where the injection should be given. Which location matches?

answers.text: Directly into the chest muscles
Directly into a vein in the wrist
On the back of the neck near the spine
In the side of the thigh, about halfway between the hip and the knee

explanations.a: Chest injection is not the AHA-described location.
explanations.b: Epinephrine autoinjectors deliver intramuscularly; intravenous injection is not appropriate.
explanations.c: Neck injection is not part of any anaphylaxis treatment guidance.
explanations.d: AHA Part 10 specifies the epinephrine injection is given in the side of the thigh, about halfway between the hip and the knee.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: epinephrine through clothing bare skin both ok
questions.text: When using an epinephrine autoinjector during anaphylaxis, AHA Part 10 addresses clothing removal. What does the manual say?

answers.text: All clothing must be removed or the injection will not work
Epinephrine can be given on bare skin or through clothing
The injection must be given only through sterile draping
Clothing must be cut with sterile scissors first

explanations.a: Removing clothing wastes time during a time-critical emergency.
explanations.b: AHA Part 10 explicitly states epinephrine can be given on bare skin or through clothing.
explanations.c: Sterile preparation is not required for emergency epinephrine autoinjector use.
explanations.d: Sterile scissors are not required; ordinary clothing is fine.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: circulation shock fast heart rate cool skin low BP dizzy
questions.text: AHA Part 10 lists circulatory signs of severe allergic reaction indicating poor perfusion. Which set matches?

answers.text: Slow heart rate of 50 with warm pink skin
Normal vital signs and full alertness throughout
Very fast heart rate, changes in skin color, cool skin, reduced alertness, low blood pressure, and dizziness
High blood pressure with elevated body temperature only

explanations.a: Slow rate with warm pink skin is reassuring, not a sign of poor perfusion.
explanations.b: Normal vital signs and full alertness rule out severe poor perfusion.
explanations.c: AHA Part 10 lists very fast heart rate, changes in skin color, cool skin, not alert, low blood pressure, and dizziness as circulation findings of poor perfusion in anaphylaxis.
explanations.d: High BP with fever is not the AHA-described shock pattern of anaphylaxis.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: debrief evaluate CPR performance emotions team dynamics
questions.text: AHA Part 5 describes the purpose of debriefing after a resuscitation. Which set of goals best matches?

answers.text: Assign blame to the team member responsible for errors
Document only the time of arrest for the medical record
Evaluate process and CPR performance, reflect on team dynamics, provide education for quality improvement, and process emotions
Conduct a financial review of the resources used

explanations.a: Blame assignment is not the AHA-described purpose; debriefing is about learning, not punishment.
explanations.b: Documentation is a separate task from debriefing.
explanations.c: AHA Part 5 says debriefing is an opportunity for evaluating process and CPR performance, reflecting on team dynamics, providing education for quality improvement, and processing emotions after a stressful event.
explanations.d: Financial review is not the AHA-described debriefing purpose.

questions.name: Special Emergencies and Recovery
questions.keyword: rescuer psychological support resiliency burnout prevention
questions.text: After a long, unsuccessful resuscitation attempt, a team leader reviews AHA recovery and survivorship guidance with the team. Which statement most accurately reflects that guidance?

answers.text: Recovery support is only relevant for the patient, never for rescuers
Rescuers and caregivers may benefit from psychological support, resiliency, burnout prevention, and effective debriefing
Family members of survivors should not be involved in any recovery activities
Debriefing should be delayed at least 6 months after the event

explanations.a: AHA Part 2 extends recovery and survivorship considerations beyond the patient to caregivers and rescuers.
explanations.b: AHA Part 2 explicitly notes rescuers and caregivers may benefit from psychological support, resiliency, burnout prevention, and effective debriefing.
explanations.c: Family members are part of the support network; AHA encourages a multimodal recovery approach.
explanations.d: Effective debriefing is recommended after the event, not delayed by months.
